traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Guttiferae: leaves usually opposite, sometimes alternate or whorled; leaves simple; margins entire; veins pinnate; stipules present or absent; plants hermaphrodite, monoecious, polygamous or dioecious; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems woody or herbaceous; flowers in cymes, in umbels or in panicles, rarely solitary; flowers actinomorphic; perianth sepals and petals or spiral; fruit capsule, berry or drupe; stamens (3-) 5 to 100; carpels (1-) 3 to 5 (-13). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.flowering_position.note: DELTA Guttiferae (read 2026-10-16): inflorescences terminal (Garcinia also axillary, my knowledge).

traits.flower_merosity.note: DELTA Guttiferae (read 2026-10-16): petals 2-6 (to 14). Typical 4 is my weighting from Garcinia (~400 of ~750 spp.).

traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Guttiferae (read 2026-10-17): simple, undivided lamina with entire margins; Wikipedia Clusia: simple, entire.

traits.sexual_system.note: DELTA Guttiferae (read 2026-10-17) lists bisexual, monoecious, dioecious and polygamous plants without weighting (its bisexual records are mostly Hypericaceae, now apart). Wikipedia (read 2026-10-17): Clusiaceae ~750 spp; Garcinia (416 spp) dioecious; Clusia (327 spp) unisexual flowers on separate plants. The two genera hold nearly the whole family.
